alignments.note: Verbless clause with an adjectival predicate and a nominal subject: rule 53 gives the supplied copula to the predicate adjective, as `ὅμοια` → *were like* does, and rule 63 refuses to read it off the ASV's word order merely because *Blessed is* stands together. Head on *Blessed*, the word glossing the lexeme.
`ἀνήρ` is anarthrous, so no article competes for the determiner slot and the supplied *the* is an ordinary rule 7 helper on the word it determines, under rule 51's anarthrous clause.
Relative pronoun with an expressed antecedent, rendered by the archaic relativizer *that*. No nominal is supplied, so rule 77 does not arise.
Finite present indicative standing alone.
Anarthrous accusative object with no determiner supplied.
Causal `ὅτι` realized by the word introducing its English clause, *for*, under rule 40's principle. Not recitative and not a dropped complementizer, so rule 43 does not apply.

Circumstantial participle recast as a finite subordinate clause. Rule 86: a participle is a source token that licenses a supplied subordinator, so *when* is an ordinary rule 7 helper rather than `added`, and the supplied subject and auxiliary ride with it under rules 7 and 9. Head on *been*, the word realizing `γίνομαι`, not on the auxiliary *hath* (rule 17).

`δόκιμος` is a predicate adjective of the participial clause — *having become approved* — so the copular material belongs to `γενόμενος` and *approved* stands alone. Split under rule 2, both pieces being independently recoverable. The competing reading takes English *hath been approved* as one passive verb phrase and puts *approved* with `γενόμενος`; that ignores that `δόκιμος` is a separate lexeme with its own English word, which rule 26 makes the reason to split.
Rule 9: the inflected future takes its English subject and auxiliary, headed on the lexical verb *receive* rather than on *shall*.
Article surfacing as English *the* under rule 19; split from its noun under rule 26.
Head noun standing bare behind its own article.

The ASV gives *life* no determiner, so this article has no *the* to anchor and is `unrepresented` under rule 23; rule 21 forbids leaving a bare *of* on it, so the case preposition stays with the noun, exactly as `τῆς εἰρήνης` → *of peace* does. The competing reading gives *of the* to the article, but no *the* is written.
Genitive noun rendered *of + noun*, the case preposition riding along; rule 17 heads it on the noun.
Relative pronoun rendered *which*, its antecedent *crown* expressed, with no supplied nominal, so rule 77 does not arise.

Article governing the expressed subject noun of the relative clause, surfacing as *the* under rule 19. The ASV italicizes *the Lord*, but the selected reading r01 of SBLGNT.JAS.1.12.v002 covers s016–s017, the packet carries no `FALLBACK EXCLUDED BY EVIDENCE` mark, and rule 11 makes the italics evidence rather than a verdict; rule 12 forbids re-deciding the text here.
Subject noun of the relative clause, split from its article under rule 26. A title rather than a name, and the ASV writes the determiner, so rule 23's article-before-a-name case does not apply.
Finite aorist standing alone; its subject is expressed by s016–s017, so no supplied subject rides here.

Substantival article before a participle: rule 32 gives it the pronoun and nothing else, so *them* is the article's and *that love* stays with the participle. The dative case preposition *to* rides with the article under rule 21, as it does in `ὡς τῷ κυρίῳ` → *as unto the Lord*. Rule 90 is not this case, the ASV writing more than one English word for the pair.
Participle carrying the supplied relativizer under rule 32 — the article governs no expressed head noun, which is rule 31's test — headed on the lexical verb *love*.
Accusative object pronoun of the participle.

review_notes: Kept the accepted alignment's units and heads unchanged; the only substantive edit is to s019's note, which cited rule 31 for the relativizer. Rule 31 is only the test (does the article govern an expressed head noun?); here it governs none, so the split and the relativizer's placement on the participle are rule 32's, and the note now says so. No id membership, status or head moved.
Partition verified: s001–s020 and t001–t029 each appear exactly once. Units are presented in target order, so s008 precedes s007 and s016–s017 precede s015.

s012 is the only `unrepresented` unit. A reference comparison will report it as a disagreement; rule 21's determinerless case (*of peace*, *by prayer*) decides it, since the ASV writes *of life* with no *the* for the article to anchor.

t022/t023 carry ASV addition markup. The variant line selects r01 of SBLGNT.JAS.1.12.v002, which covers s015–s017, and carries no `FALLBACK EXCLUDED BY EVIDENCE` mark, so rule 97 is not in play in either direction and rule 11 keeps *the Lord* aligned rather than `added`. Rule 12 bars reopening the textual question here even though the ASV's own base evidently lacked `ὁ κύριος`.

s007/s008 were split rather than bundled: *approved* recovers `δόκιμος` and *when he hath been* recovers `γενόμενος`. The competing reading — treating *hath been approved* as one English passive verb phrase on the participle — is recorded in the s007 note per rule 16.
*when* at t009 is a helper, not `added`: rule 86's test asks whether a source token licenses the subordinator, and the participle `γενόμενος` is such a token.
